html:
A goldsmith of Mainz who made printing with movable metal type practical in Europe, around 1450. His Bible of the 1450s, the Gutenberg Bible, began the age of print in the West.

Movable type itself was not new: Bi Sheng had made it from clay in China around 1040, and Korea printed books with metal type in the 1300s. Gutenberg's achievement was a full system: a hand mould for casting many identical letters fast, a metal mix of lead, tin and antimony, an oil-based ink, and a screw press adapted from those used for wine and paper.

He borrowed heavily to set up his shop. His backer Johann Fust sued him around 1455 and took over much of the business, and Gutenberg died in 1468 with little to show for it.

Printing spread fast: by 1500 presses in some 250 towns had turned out millions of books, and by 1539 there was a press in Mexico. Cheap print spread Renaissance learning, science and above all Martin Luther's pamphlets, which drove the Reformation.
sum: A goldsmith of Mainz who made printing with movable metal type practical in Europe, around 1450. His Bible of the 1450s, the Gutenberg Bible, began the age of print in the West.
